app/next.config.ts:5 — top-level turbopack.root, a stable documented config option (formerly experimental.turbo, renamed in 15.3)
app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:11,98 — Promise-based params/searchParams, the standard stable signature in Next 16
app/src/app/layout.tsx:1-19 — Metadata/Viewport exports, Link: all long-stable

reach.rationale: The app is built exclusively on long-stable APIs; even the newest thing it touches (connection()) has been stable for about two years, so nothing qualifies as experimental or recently-stable.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:40 — connection() is called from exactly one place, inside the single api() wrapper every page goes through
app/next.config.ts:1-9 — the only config-level choice (turbopack.root) sits in a 9-line config file, trivially removable
containment.rationale: Nothing needs containing, and even the borderline call is centralized in one data-access module, so any future change would be a one-file edit.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:32,40 — cache:'no-store' fetch already forces dynamic rendering, so connection() is redundant rather than justified; harmless belt-and-braces
app/next.config.ts:5 — turbopack.root exists only to silence the monorepo/workspace-root ambiguity (app/ lives inside a larger repo), a documented legitimate use
justification.rationale: No experimental or preview APIs are used at all; the two modern-ish touches are either justified by the repo layout or cheaply redundant, none are novelty.

findings.issue: await connection() is redundant: the fetch on line 32 uses cache:'no-store', which already opts every route that calls api() into dynamic rendering, and the docs say connection() is only needed when no request-time API is used.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the call, or keep it as an explicit, commented guarantee that data is always fetched at request time regardless of future fetch-caching defaults; either way it's a one-line change.

findings.issue: turbopack.root with import.meta.dirname is stable but has a known ecosystem pitfall with ESM next.config.ts on some build pipelines (Vercel issue #16405); the app is served via npm start so it's unaffected here.
findings.suggestion: Keep as-is; add a brief comment noting why the root is pinned (app directory nested inside the repo) so a future contributor doesn't remove it and hit the ambiguous-workspace-root warning.

summary: The app uses zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, and no experimental config flags. Its only notably modern touches — connection(), the top-level turbopack config key, and Promise-based params — have all been stable since Next 15/16 and are confirmed stable in the current v16 docs. Risk of framework churn breaking this code is minimal; the single redundant connection() call is the only cleanup worth mentioning.
